title: Active Record Pattern / Domain-Managed Persistence
pattern: Mixing core business rules with persistence methods (`save`, `delete`, `update`) in the same domain structure.
why_bad: It violates persistence ignorance and single responsibility principle. Any modification to the database schema or driver forces changes and recompilation of core business logic.
detection: Method names `save`, `delete`, `insert_into`, `update` defined directly on core business domain structs and taking database connection parameters.
counterexample: Low-level data gateway structures whose explicit, sole purpose is persistence.
source: *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* by Martin Fowler (p. 160); *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (p. 226).
